topic: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres: Linking Cones to Ellipses
target_audience: High school students (Advanced Geometry) and undergraduate math enthusiasts

sections.title: The Mystery of the Sliced Cone
lecture_lines: Conic sections appear when a plane slices a cone.
Tilting the plane transforms a circle into an ellipse.
How can we prove this shape is truly an ellipse?
animations: A gold cone (#FFD700) is sliced horizontally by a light blue plane (#ADD8E6), forming a circle.
The plane tilts, and the intersection curve becomes an orange-red (#FF4500) ellipse.
Two magenta points (#FF00FF) appear inside the ellipse, representing the mysterious foci.
The question 'PF1 + PF2 = Constant?' appears near the ellipse.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Two-Tangent Theorem
lecture_lines: Two tangents from a point to a sphere are equal.
Think of it like an ice cream cone shape.
These equal lengths are the key to our proof.
animations: A white point P (#FFFFFF) sits outside a blue sphere (#00BFFF).
Two yellow lines (#FFFF00) extend from P to touch the sphere at A and B.
Segments PA and PB are highlighted; labels 'L' appear to show they are equal.

sections.title: Enter the Dandelin Spheres
lecture_lines: We place two spheres inside the cone.
Each touches the cone and the slicing plane.
The contact points on the plane are the foci.
animations: The cone (#FFD700) and tilted plane (#ADD8E6) return.
A small lime sphere (#7FFF00) expands above the plane until tangent to cone and plane.
A larger cyan sphere (#00FFFF) expands below the plane until tangent to cone and plane.
The contact points on the plane are marked as F1 and F2 in magenta (#FF00FF).

sections.title: The 'Aha!' Moment: The Geometric Proof
lecture_lines: Pick any point on the elliptical slice.
Distance to focus equals distance to the tangent circle.
Sum of distances equals the segment between tangent circles.
This segment length is constant along the cone's surface.
Thus, PF1 plus PF2 is always constant.
animations: A white point P (#FFFFFF) is selected on the orange-red ellipse.
Segments PF1 (hot pink, #FF69B4) and PF2 (dodger blue, #1E90FF) are drawn.
Lines extend from P along the cone's surface to the tangency circles at Q1 and Q2.
PF1 is colored same as PQ1; PF2 same as PQ2, showing their equality.
The sum PF1+PF2 is shown as the constant segment Q1Q2.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Harmony
lecture_lines: Dandelin spheres elegantly bridge 2D and 3D geometry.
This proof applies to all conic sections.
These geometric principles guide orbits in space.
animations: The 3D construction fades out, leaving the 2D ellipse and foci.
The ellipse morphs into a parabola and then a hyperbola.
An elliptical orbit appears around a planet at one focus (#FFFF00).
